title: Secrets escrow & key handoff discussion with Helix Bios
summary: Customer (Helix Bios) needs clarification on BYOK/HSM key handoff, escrow options, dual-control for rotation, and audit trails. Redwood SE walked through supported HSMs, PKCS#11/CloudHSM connectivity, and suggested a two-phase pilot: test network connectivity + attestation, then a delegated key import and rotation runbook. Action items agreed: share BYOK playbook, schedule HSM connectivity test window, and provide SOC2/ISO artifacts.
next_steps: Redwood to share BYOK + HSM playbook link and sample PKCS#11 config (Priya)
Schedule 2-hour connectivity test with Helix network team (Michael)
Helix to provide list of data residency regions and legal constraints (Dr. Patel)
Exchange SOC2 Type II report and HSM attestation docs (Redwood ops)
Create runbook for emergency key-escrow recovery and sign-off (joint)
action_items: Priya Nair: Send BYOK/HSM playbook and sample PKCS#11 config by 2025-03-05
Michael Chen: Propose 2 connectivity test slots next week by 2025-03-06
Dr. Lara Patel: Share list of required regions and any export controls by 2025-03-07
Alyssa Kim: Provide network ACLs and firewall contact for the test by 2025-03-05
header: Date: 2025-03-03 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Michael Chen, Priya Nair (Redwood) — Dr. Lara Patel, Miguel Santos, Alyssa Kim, Tom Hsu (Helix Bios)
transcript:
[00:00] Michael Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Michael from Redwood — AE — and Priya our SE. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Dr. Lara Patel: Lara here, CISO at Helix.
[00:11] Miguel Santos: Miguel, cloud eng.
[00:13] Alyssa Kim: Alyssa, SRE.
[00:15] Tom Hsu: Tom, legal.
[00:18] Michael Chen: Awesome. The goal today is to walk through BYOK/hsm key handoff pattern, escrow options, and audit logging for Private deployments. Priya will run tech details.
[00:29] Priya Nair: Hi folks. Quick agenda, I'll cover supported HSMs, connectivity patterns (PKCS11, CloudHSM), the delegated import flow, and rotation/escrow best practices. Then Q&A.
[00:40] Miguel Santos: Real quick — we run most workloads in eu-west-1 and us-east-1, data residency is tight for patient records; we need keys to never leave region X.
[00:48] Priya Nair: Understood. Redwood Private supports region-bound key stores and we can integrate with customer-managed HSMs in a VPC or with AWS CloudHSM in region. Note — when you use CloudHSM the HSM itself is region-bound.
[01:01] Dr. Lara Patel: We also have a mandate for dual-control key import and a requirement that private keys never be exported once imported. Can Redwood support split knowledge and non-exportable keys?
[01:11] Priya Nair: Yes. For HSM-backed keys we set 'non-exportable' at import and use PKCS#11 handles. Split knowledge is usually implemented by having two operators perform parts of the import with quorum or via HSM vendor tooling — e.g., Thales/Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) workflows. We'll share examples.
[01:26] Alyssa Kim: Can we do an escrow? Meaning if someone leaves or an HSM fails, we want an escape hatch with strict controls.
[01:33] Priya Nair: Escrow typically has two flavors: 1) Redwood-managed escrow where we hold a wrapped backup under additional encryption and strict access logs; 2) customer-managed escrow where keys are escrowed to your vault (recommended for high regulation). Both support multi-signature and time-based access. We'll send the playbook.
[01:49] Miguel Santos: Is the escrow key itself stored in an HSM? We need FIPS-validated flow and full attestation.
[01:57] Priya Nair: Yes, escrow keys can be in an HSM and attestations are available. Redwood can provide HSM attestation docs; if you require FIPS 140-2/3 we support compatible HSMs (AWS CloudHSM, Thales Luna, Azure Key Vault HSM). Attestation is normally a signed statement from the HSM provider — we can surface that.
[02:10] Tom Hsu: From a legal perspective we need the chain of custody and audit logs retained 7 years. Do you provide immutable audit logs and exportable evidence?
[02:19] Michael Chen: Redwood Console includes per-key audit logs, admin actions, and token-level traces. For Private we can ship logs to customer SIEM or to an S3 bucket in your account for retention policies.
[02:28] Dr. Lara Patel: What about key rotation? Automatic rotation? Manual? Need a safe rollback plan.
[02:35] Priya Nair: We recommend a staged rotation: generate new key in HSM, test decrypt/encrypt with canary workloads, then switch routing. For non-exportable keys we do an alias switch rather than key export. For emergency rollback we use the escrow copy under emergency escrow protocol with dual approvals. We'll include the runbook.
[02:52] Miguel Santos: Performance — any latency hit using HSM for every sign/verify? Our inference paths are latency-sensitive.
[03:00] Priya Nair: We avoid HSM on the token path for per-token ops. Typical pattern: use HSM for key material management and wrap a short-lived symmetric data key used by runtime. The runtime uses the symmetric key (kept in memory / KV cache) for per-request encrypt/decrypt. HSM ops happen at rotation or when issuing wrapped data keys. So negligible per-token latency.
[03:20] Alyssa Kim: That 'KV cash' — sorry — KV cache — how does that interact with restart/eviction?
[03:27] Priya Nair: Yeah, KV cache. The sequence cache and data key caching has TTLs and we persist minimal state; on restart we rehydrate with previously wrapped keys which the runtime unwraps via HSM during init. We'll put config knobs in the playbook.
[03:40] Dr. Lara Patel: About SSO/RBAC: who can trigger key rotation or escrow retrieval in Redwood Console? Can we map to our IdP groups?
[03:48] Michael Chen: Yes, we integrate with SAML SSO and SCIM so you can sync groups. RBAC is role-based: Admins, KeyOps, ReadOnly. KeyOps can request rotation but the actual escrow retrieval requires dual-approval and will generate an auditable workflow.
[04:02] Tom Hsu: A follow-up on proof: do you provide independent attestations for your key-handling process?
[04:08] Priya Nair: We bundle SOC2 Type II and relevant ISO artifacts. For HSM attestation we can include the HSM vendor's attestation certs and a digest of the import session. We'll share redacted examples.
[04:20] Miguel Santos: Are there sample configurations for PKCS#11 and CloudHSM clients? We run a hardened bastion and strict egress rules.
[04:29] Priya Nair: Yes — sample PKCS#11 config, CloudHSM client settings, and required ports/UDP/TCP rules. We'll also provide a connectivity checklist for the bastion test.
[04:40] Michael Chen: Quick demo idea — after we share the playbook, we propose a 2-hour lab: step 1 network connectivity + attestation, step 2 key import into your test HSM, step 3 set up runbook for rotation. Does that sound reasonable?
[04:53] Dr. Lara Patel: Yes. Prefer next week morning windows.
[04:57] Miguel Santos: Also want to test the worst-case: HSM loss and full recovery using escrow under our legal sign-off.
[05:06] Priya Nair: We'll include that recovery scenario. For recovery you'll have an escrow envelope encrypted under a customer recovery key; retrieval requires two Helix approvers and one Redwood compliance approver in the default model — this is configurable.
[05:20] Alyssa Kim: Recording question — audit logs of who requested the escrow, who approved, and the exact commands executed are exported?
[05:27] Michael Chen: Yes, the audit trail includes timestamps, user identities (via SSO), the action, and the underlying operation id. We can provide an export in JSONL for ingestion to Splunk/ELK or send to your S3.
[05:40] Tom Hsu: Any legal restrictions around key export to countries? We might have to avoid certain jurisdictions.
[05:46] Priya Nair: That's why region-bound HSMs and customer-managed escrow in your account are recommended. We also support geo-fencing of escrow copies. We'll capture specifics when you share the list of restricted jurisdictions.
[05:59] Dr. Lara Patel: About BYOK import — do you require us to use a particular format? We have existing key material in Azure Key Vault. Can we import via wrapped key?
[06:08] Priya Nair: Yes, wrapped key import is supported. We accept standard formats; for cloud key exchanges we can ingest a wrapped key object. We also support a transit-style approach where your AKV can issue a wrapped key to Redwood's import endpoint under a mutual TLS session.
[06:22] Miguel Santos: Mutual TLS — do you handle cert rotation? We prefer mTLS with rotating certs and short lifetimes.
[06:27] Priya Nair: mTLS with cert rotation is supported. For Private deployments we can host the import endpoint in your VPC; certificates are managed by your PKI. We'll document the CSR process.
[06:42] Michael Chen: Quick pause for questions.
[06:45] Speaker 6: Sorry — are there additional charges for HSM-backed keys?
[06:50] Michael Chen: For Dedicated/Private deployments there's typically an incremental cost due to reserved HSM capacity or CloudHSM hourly charges. We'll include a cost estimate in the follow-up.
[07:00] Dr. Lara Patel: One more on retention: we need proof that audit logs are immutable. Is there an append-only write mechanism or WORM?
[07:08] Priya Nair: You can configure write-once S3 buckets in your account (S3 Object Lock) or route logs to a SIEM with immutability policies. Redwood's console stores audit events but for regulatory-grade immutability we recommend customer-side WORM.
[07:22] Miguel Santos: Let's talk timeline — must be in pilot by end of Q2. Can Redwood meet that?
[07:28] Michael Chen: Yes. Pilot plan: week 1 connectivity and attestation, week 2 import and rotation runbook, week 3 integration with apps and telemetry. We'll map out milestones in the next email.
[07:40] Dr. Lara Patel: For the pilot do you have a checklist for legal sign-offs? Tom, can you coordinate with them?
[07:46] Tom Hsu: Sure. We'll want the escrow contract, SLAs for recovery, and nondisclosure around key custody.
[07:53] Priya Nair: We'll add a sample escrow agreement and SLA template.
[07:59] Miguel Santos: Any blockers for Helix to run the connectivity test? We'll need a test HSM instance and a secured bastion.
[08:06] Michael Chen: Redwood can provision a CloudHSM test instance if you prefer, or we can test against your staging HSM. Which do you prefer?
[08:14] Dr. Lara Patel: Prefer our staging HSM behind our firewall. We'll provide bastion details.
[08:19] Priya Nair: Great. We'll need egress rules and the bastion public key for the connectivity window.
[08:26] Michael Chen: I'll email proposed time slots.
[08:29] Alyssa Kim: Small note — our compliance team requires a cryptographic policy doc that lists algorithms and key sizes.
[08:36] Priya Nair: We'll attach our allowed algorithms matrix (RSA 3072+, ECC P-256/P-384, AES-256 GCM, and allowed key-wrapping primitives).
[08:48] Dr. Lara Patel: Thanks. Any final things before we wrap?
[08:52] Michael Chen: Recap — Redwood to share BYOK/HSM playbook, sample configs, SOC2/ISO artifacts redacted, schedule 2-hour connectivity test. Helix to share region constraints, bastion details, and staging HSM creds for the test. Action items recorded and we'll follow up by email.
[09:06] Miguel Santos: Sounds good.
[09:08] Tom Hsu: Thanks all.
[09:10] Michael Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up. End call.

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., 'KV cash' for KV cache); speaker 6 label used once due to recording capture. References shared: https://docs.redwood.ai/kms/byok (playbook), https://drive.company/helix/pilot-plan (shared deck).
